sentences.text: The petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 got married on 09.03.2015 at Delhi according to Hindu rites and customs and out of their marriage one male child, namely, Advik Aggarwal was born on 03.06.2016, who at present is under the care and custody of the respondent no. 2.
The petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 due to matrimonial differences started to live separately w.e.f. 04.05.2018 without any cohabitation.
5. The respondent no. 2 filed petitions under section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 and under section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner no
. 4 also filed a civil suit bearing no. 577/2017 titled as Satya Prakash Gupta V Anuj Gupta & Anr. stated to be pending in the court of Sh. Vishal Pahuja, SCJ, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi.

entities.text: Satya Prakash Gupta V Anuj Gupta & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is stated that these petitions/civil suit have already been withdrawn by the concerned parties.

6. The respondent no.2 due to matrimonial differences, lodged a complaint against the petitioners before CAW Cell, Outer District, which was culminated into registration of FIR bearing no.0613/2020 under sections 498A/406/354A/377/506/509 at P.S. Laxmi Nagar wherein the petitioners were implicated.
The investigation is still pending and the charge-sheet has not been filed.
The petitioners no.2 to 5 are the family members/relatives of the petitioner no.1.
The petitioner no.2 is not present and is exempted from personal appearance as her identity is not disputed.
The petitioners no. 1 and 3 are present in court.
The petitioners no. 4 and 5 are appearing through video-conferencing.
The petitioners no.1 and 3 to 5 and the respondent no.2 are identified by SI Khushbu Singh, P.S. Laxmi Nagar as well as by their respective counsel.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 21/09/2023 at 21:56:58 7.

The petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 have settled their disputes vide Mutual Settlement/Memorandum of Understanding stated to be executed on 25.08.2021 whereby they have agreed to dissolve their marriage by way of mutual consent as per section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

The petitioner no.1 has agreed to pay Rs. 21,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty One Lacs Only) to the respondent no.2 towards full and final satisfaction of her claims/legal entitlements (past,
present and future) arising out of marriage between the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no. 2 including permanent alimony/maintenance/istridhan etc. and other miscellaneous and legal expenses.
It is stated that the petitioner no.1 has already paid Rs.19,00,000/- to the respondent no.2, which is acknowledged by the respondent no.2.

The petitioner no.1 also delivered a demand draft bearing no. 040338 dated 18.09.2023 drawn on HDFC Bank amounting to Rs.2,00,000/- to the counsel for the respondent no.2 on behalf of the respondent no. 2 towards payment of balance settled amount, which is accepted by the respondent no.2.
8.

The marriage between the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 has been dissolved by way of decree of divorce by mutual consent as per section 13B (2) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 by the court of Sh. Nareh Kumar Malhotra, Judge, Family Courts, East District, Karkardooma Courts,
Delhi vide judgment dated 19.04.2022 in petition bearing HMA no.119/2022 titled as Victim and Anuj Gupta And Ors vs State & Anr on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178944189/
